chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Zurara who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Qiblah of the one confused, so he (peace be upon him) said: He prays wherever he desires.

key_terms.الْمُتَحَيِّر: The confused one, one who is uncertain or perplexed
key_terms.قِبْلَة: Qiblah, the direction of prayer towards the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Muslim who is unsure of the Qiblah direction?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) grants a concession to the 'mutahayyir' (one confused about the Qiblah), ruling that they may pray in any direction without penalty. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of 'sahh al-salat' (validity of prayer) in cases of genuine uncertainty, distinguishing it from deliberate deviation. The ruling emphasizes ease and removes the burden of exhaustive search when the heart is genuinely perplexed.
